transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer, Priya Natarajan, Daniel Cho (Redwood); Jared Kim, Lina Ortega, Marcus Liu, Sofia Park (RadiantCore)

Summary: quick intake and kickoff to align on network access, security gating items, staging provisioning, pilot criteria and immediate action items.

[00:00] Alex Mercer: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'll keep us tight on time. alex from redwood here, priya our se, daniel cs lead. how are folks at radiantcore?
[00:08] Jared Kim: good thanks alex, excited to get this rolling. we reviewed the docs, we've got some constraints around network and data retention to discuss.
[00:15] Alex Mercer: perfect, goal today is intake not delivery—map the runway. priya will walk through tech checklist then we'll capture owners.
[00:22] Priya Natarajan: yeah hi all, quick intro—i'm priya, i do dedicated and private rollouts. we'll cover three areas: access & networking, security/compliance, and staging + pilot tests. i'll try not to nerd out too hard but, you know, a little nerd-out is inevitable.
[00:40] Marcus Liu: sounds good, just so you know our timeline: pilot target is january 20th, production in february, but we need gating from security.
[00:49] Alex Mercer: noted, jan 20th pilot — ok. lina, who on your side will own VPC setup?
[00:55] Lina Ortega: that's me, devops lead. we run aws accounts per environment. we prefer VPC peering but can do private link if needed. also we have an on-prem datacenter behind a proxy for model inputs in some cases.
[01:10] Priya Natarajan: great, we can support both VPC peering and private link; for private deployments we hand over an agent and customer manages KMS in their HSM, or we plug into their KMS via IAM roles — sometimes the wording in our docs gets munged, pax, pox... — i mean sometimes names get swapped.
[01:28] Sofia Park: quick interruption — is there a standard KMS integration pattern or do we need an HSM? we use Thales currently for keys.
[01:34] Priya Natarajan: we support external KMS like Thales or cloud KMS; for on-prem HSM we do an integration point and keep only wrapped keys. i'd flag that for legal but it's doable. we'll share the KMS integration guide.
[01:47] Jared Kim: ok, good. what about audit logs and retention? we need 7 years for some records.
[01:53] Daniel Cho: hey jared, daniel on cs. for audit logs we capture request-level metadata, model version, route, tokens and error traces; retention is configurable depending on your plan. seven years is long — we usually store raw transcripts for 90-365 days and export to your s3 for long-term archival. we can automate snapshots to your bucket for longer retention.
[02:12] Sofia Park: and is data encrypted at rest in transit? we need TLS + customer-managed keys for rest encryption.
[02:18] Priya Natarajan: yes tls in transit and rest is encrypted; customer-managed keys supported. sometimes our docs say KVS cache instead of KV cache which threw a sec engineer earlier — small typo but causes confusion.
[02:32] Lina Ortega: ha yeah i saw "KVS" noted. ok about networking, we will provide CIDR ranges, egress rules and proxy details. we also have a strict egress policy — only certain subnets can talk out. will that break batching or streaming?
[02:46] Priya Natarajan: batching is internal to the runtime; it shouldn't require extra egress. streaming responses will maintain long-lived connections; if you run a proxy that times out after 30s that could be an issue. we can tune chunk intervals but ideally you allow longer idle for those routes.
[03:03] Marcus Liu: regarding models, we plan to start with open models—llama variants and a Red-verified small model. is model pinning available?
[03:12] Priya Natarajan: yes model pinning for the route, you can pin a specific model version and configure rollout policies like canary or A/B or automatic fallback to a lower-cost family. sometimes the console labels get shortened to "pin v1" which confused folks, but it's per-route in the API.
[03:28] Alex Mercer: also we'll seed a staging model for you. who will own the test prompts?
[03:34] Marcus Liu: i'll own gathering 10 canonical prompts and expected outputs. we'll share those by sunday.
[03:40] Alex Mercer: great, that's one of our action items.
[03:44] [05:00] (brief pause while folks shuffle notes)
[05:15] Priya Natarajan: next, observability — our console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency histograms, and per-route traces. we recommend adding a few tracing hooks: request_id, user_id (or anon id), and prompt_hash. that helps QA and cost attribution.
[05:35] Lina Ortega: can we get those logs to our datadog?
[05:38] Daniel Cho: yes, we have a datadog export and a streaming webhook for events; you can also pull raw events from S3.
[05:44] Sofia Park: on compliance, we need SOC2 type II and ISO docs; can you share current attestation?
[05:49] Alex Mercer: yes we'll share SOC2 and ISO PDFs and a short compliance package. also a small note: we have a private deployment option if you need total isolation; it's a different cadence and license.
[06:02] Jared Kim: is private necessary? we prefer hosted but must satisfy security. if you support customer-managed KMS and private peering to a hosted tenant is that good enough for security?
[06:13] Priya Natarajan: often yes — hosted with VPC peering and customer KMS hits the requirement. private is for fully on-prem or air-gapped. we should loop legal/infosec to validate.
[06:24] Marcus Liu: ok, we'll evaluate.
[06:28] [08:10] Priya Natarajan: onto staging provisioning: we will create a staging org tenant with the same model config as prod, seed a small dataset for smoke tests, and give you creds for a read-only service account + an ops key for smoke testing. Lina, we need network allowlist and a certificate thumbprint (if you are pinning certs) to open peering.
[08:36] Lina Ortega: certificate pinning is possible, we use internal CA — we can generate a cert chain for you.
[08:42] Alex Mercer: perfect. we'll document exact cert format in the runbook.
[08:47] Priya Natarajan: for benchmarks we usually run a 30-minute synthetic throughput job and a latency tail test at different seq lengths. that catches kernel scheduling and batching inefficiencies. we noticed... um earlier on some customer calls seq len mismatch caused kv cache thrashing — the shorthand in our notebook says "kv thrash" and that can alarm folks.
[09:10] Marcus Liu: what's the expected cost signal during pilot? we need unit economics for product planning.
[09:16] Daniel Cho: we'll output cost per 1k tokens per route and show cost lift by turning on prefix caching or quantization. priya will run a sample with your prompts to estimate.
[09:28] Priya Natarajan: note on quantization — model fidelity sometimes shifts; we recommend AB tests on quality and have evaluation harness integrated into the console so you can track regressions.
[09:40] Sofia Park: any risk of data exfiltration when using caching?
[09:43] Priya Natarajan: caching is turned off by default for sensitive routes; if enabled we do per-tenant prefix scoping and encrypted in-flight. we also support deterministic scrubbers in the pipeline.
[09:55] Jared Kim: good. ok quick question on SSO — can you integrate with our okta SAML?
[09:59] Alex Mercer: yes SAML/SSO is standard; we also do SCIM for provisioning. we'll share SSO setup doc. daniel will help with onboarding seats.
[10:10] Daniel Cho: for CSM handover, we'll run a 2-week ramp: week one staging + smoke, week two pilot and uplift. after that we schedule a go/no-go for production.
[10:22] Marcus Liu: that lines up.
[10:24] [12:05] (phone beep, background)
[12:10] Priya Natarajan: ok for the immediate technical checklist i captured: 1) network allowlist + proxy details, 2) cert chain or thumbprint, 3) CIDR and egress policy, 4) KMS vendor details and integration approach, 5) success criteria + sample prompts. can someone confirm?
[12:26] Lina Ortega: i'll take network allowlist, cert chain and proxy info.
[12:29] Sofia Park: i'll take KMS and retention requirements.
[12:33] Marcus Liu: i'll finalize success criteria + prompts.
[12:36] Alex Mercer: and alex will send the runbook + credentials template. agreed.
[12:40] [14:00] Priya Natarajan: one blocker spotted: your proxy times out after 45s on long-poll connections; if any of your use cases expect >45s streaming we need to either tune the proxy or add a tcp keepalive shim. can you check if streams will be long?
[14:18] Lina Ortega: most streams are short, but we do have a support flow that could stream longer if a user is receiving a long consolidated explanation. we can increase timeout in staging for the pilot.
[14:27] Alex Mercer: great, plan to test streaming in staging early.
[14:30] [20:00] (longer discussion about internal runbook formatting and who gets what permission)
[20:15] Daniel Cho: ops notes — we'll provision roles: Viewer, Operator, Admin. we recommend Operator for your devops and Viewer for product. scim will handle seat provisioning.
[20:29] Sofia Park: RBAC mappings look good; we might want a custom role for auditing.
[20:33] Priya Natarajan: we can support a custom role with read-only audit access.
[20:38] Jared Kim: ok that's helpful.
[20:42] [25:00] Alex Mercer: let's recap: owners and dates. alex will send runbook by 12/17; lina provide networking by 12/20; marcus provide prompts by 12/19; priya to prep staging benchmark scripts by 12/21; sofia to confirm KMS vendor and retention by 12/21. redwood to provision staging and seed models by 12/22. pilot target 2027-01-20.
[25:55] Marcus Liu: any concerns re: cost? we want a ballpark before the pilot to decide traffic caps.
[26:02] Daniel Cho: we'll provide a cost estimate based on pilot prompts and token counts, include cost sensitivity to batching and quantization.
[26:10] [30:00] (wrap up)
[30:12] Alex Mercer: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the runbook and security package. if legal needs the NDA amendment, daniel will coordinate.
[30:22] Jared Kim: great thanks, talk soon.
[30:25] Meeting ended

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few misheard product words (eg "KVS cache" vs "KV cache") and occasional speaker switches; we've kept the conversational flow intact.

References shared: onboarding_runbook_v1.xlsx (link), staging_benchmark_template.ipynb (link), SOC2_snapshot_2026.pdf (link)
